title: Maths seen and heard from one parse, in RISE Live and Composer
acceptance: Every form a model writes maths in is found: $…$ (never money such as $5 and $10), $$…$$, \(…\), \[…\], TeX in backticks, and bare TeX that begins with a known command; file paths and \n stay prose (src/core/math-corpus.js).

Each formula is parsed once by KaTeX: typeset for the eye with MathML beside it for a screen reader, and said by the Speech Rule Engine in ClearSpeak from that MathML (E = ½ℏω is said 'E equals one half h bar omega'). A spoken form the model writes (say => show) still wins.
No backslash command, brace or dollar of maths is ever shown as prose or said by a voice: before the typesetter has loaded, or for TeX KaTeX refuses, both channels take a plain Unicode reading.

In a streamed Live answer a passage with maths is held until the typesetter has loaded (at most 3 s), so a formula is never shown as source and then snapped into place; the voice and the speech governor are given the same spoken words, and the formula's phrase is on screen while its speech is said.

A formula is never cut between phrases; a display equation is a phrase of its own, centred; inline maths is set at the words' x-height and keeps the line one line tall; a comma written against a formula stays against it.
A shown formula (a beat no voice says) stays at least as long as it takes to say plus 300 ms per structure, the extra at most 2.5 s (owner, 2026-10-26).
Nothing is added to the first load (63.1 KB against the 64 KB budget); KaTeX, the speech engine and its English rules load only for a reading with maths, from RISE's own assets.

A spoken formula is followed by a silence of 300 ms per structure (at most 2.5 s), with the formula on screen through it, in every voice (voices/pauses.js wraps the voice the runtime makes); the reader's hold stands it still, a seek or cancel drops it, a faster pace shortens it.

ClearSpeak is said as a person says it: a bracket around a sum is "the quantity" (2 times the quantity a plus b; the quantity a plus b, squared), any other bracket is silent (f of x comma y), |x| is "the absolute value of x", a limit is "the limit as x approaches 0 of", ∇ is "del" with "dot" and "cross", ∂ is "partial", ℏ is "h bar", and a unit written as text is said in words (meters per second).

evidence.note: The diagnosis (four causes, reproduced through the Live parser and the Current compiler; the production demo answers only about black holes and a real model needs the reader's key), the owner's three decisions of 2026-10-26 (SRE ClearSpeak; dwell as proposed; a display equation a beat of its own), and the design.

summary: Maths in RISE Live and Composer is typeset for the eye and said for the ear from one KaTeX parse (Speech Rule Engine, ClearSpeak), found in every form a model writes it and never in money, held in a stream until it can be shown and said, and set at the words' size; nothing added to the first load.
